import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Shephard's problem (a.k.a. Dürer's conjecture)

Does every convex polyhedron have a net, or simple edge-unfolding?

A (compact) convex polyhedron is the boundary of the convex hull $K$ of finitely many points of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ which do not all lie in a plane, i.e. $K$ has nonempty interior. Cutting the
boundary of $K$ along a spanning tree $T$ of the edge graph of $K$ yields a surface $K_T$: the
disjoint union of the facets of $K$, glued back together along the edges that are not in $T$.
This surface is a flat topological disk, so it can be developed isometrically into the plane.
Such a development is an *edge unfolding* of $K$. It is *simple*, and its image is a *net*, if the
developing map $K_T \to \mathbb{R}^2$ is one-to-one, i.e. the unfolded faces do not overlap.

Shephard (1975) asked whether every convex polyhedron admits a simple edge unfolding. The
conjectured answer "yes" is known as Dürer's conjecture. The problem is open.

We follow the conventions of Ghomi and Barvinok–Ghomi: an unfolding of $K_T$ is a map to the
plane which preserves distances between points of each facet, and it is simple when it is
one-to-one on all of $K_T$. In particular two distinct points of $K_T$ (for instance two copies
of a cut vertex) may not touch in the plane. The cut tree must consist of genuine edges of $K$
(not pseudo-edges, and the facets are not subdivided).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Net (polyhedron)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shephard%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sh75] Shephard, G. C., *Convex polytopes with convex nets*, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc.
  78 (1975), 389–403.
- [Gh14] Ghomi, M., *Affine unfoldings of convex polyhedra*, Geom. Topol. 18 (2014), 3055–3090.
  [arXiv:1305.3231](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.3231)
- [BG20] Barvinok, N. and Ghomi, M., *Pseudo-edge unfoldings of convex polyhedra*, Discrete
  Comput. Geom. 64 (2020), 671–689. [arXiv:1709.04944](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.04944)
-/
open scoped EuclideanGeometry
namespace ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

blocks.code:
def IsFacet (K F : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsExposed ℝ K F ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ F) = 2
blocks.docstring:
`IsFacet K F` means that `F` is a facet (a two-dimensional face) of the convex polytope
`K ⊆ ℝ³`: `F` is an exposed face of `K` whose affine span is a plane.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsExposed` and `IsExtreme` (Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Exposed / Extreme); `IsExtreme` alone was rejected because extreme subsets need not be convex (e.g. a set of several vertices), so `IsExposed` plus the dimension condition is used.
justification.name: ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture.IsFacet
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of the faces/facets of a polytope; a facet is encoded as an exposed subset with 2-dimensional affine span.

blocks.name: IsFacet
blocks.text:
/-- `IsFacet K F` means that `F` is a facet (a two-dimensional face) of the convex polytope
`K ⊆ ℝ³`: `F` is an exposed face of `K` whose affine span is a plane. -/
def IsFacet (K F : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsExposed ℝ K F ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ F) = 2

blocks.code: abbrev Facet (K : Set ℝ³) : Type := {F : Set ℝ³ // IsFacet K F}
blocks.docstring: The type of facets of the convex polytope `K ⊆ ℝ³`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `IsExposed` and `affineSpan`; `Facet` is their problem-specific combination requiring affine dimension two.
justification.name: Facet
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has exposed subsets but no polytope facet type; the cut surface needs the collection of actual polygonal facets.

blocks.name: Facet
blocks.text:
/-- The type of facets of the convex polytope `K ⊆ ℝ³`. -/
abbrev Facet (K : Set ℝ³) : Type := {F : Set ℝ³ // IsFacet K F}

blocks.code:
def edgeGraph (K : Set ℝ³) : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ) where
  Adj v w := v ≠ w ∧ IsExposed ℝ K (segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w)
  symm v w h := ⟨h.1.symm, segment_symm ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ▸ h.2⟩
  loopless _ h := h.1 rfl
blocks.docstring:
The edge graph of the convex polytope `K ⊆ ℝ³`. Its vertices are the extreme points of `K`,
and two distinct vertices `v`, `w` are adjacent when the segment `[v, w]` is an exposed face of
`K`, i.e. an edge of `K`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `SimpleGraph`, `Set.extremePoints`, `IsExposed`, and `segment`; the definition combines these without adding pseudo-edges.
justification.name: edgeGraph
justification.why_needed: No existing API constructs the actual edge graph of a finite convex hull.

blocks.name: edgeGraph
blocks.text:
/-- The edge graph of the convex polytope `K ⊆ ℝ³`. Its vertices are the extreme points of `K`,
and two distinct vertices `v`, `w` are adjacent when the segment `[v, w]` is an exposed face of
`K`, i.e. an edge of `K`. -/
def edgeGraph (K : Set ℝ³) : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ) where
  Adj v w := v ≠ w ∧ IsExposed ℝ K (segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w)
  symm v w h := ⟨h.1.symm, segment_symm ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ▸ h.2⟩
  loopless _ h := h.1 rfl

blocks.code: abbrev FacetPoint (K : Set ℝ³) : Type := Σ F : Facet K, F.1
blocks.docstring: A point of the disjoint union of the facets of `K`: a facet `F` together with a point of `F`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib has quotient and gluing infrastructure but no cut-polyhedral-surface point type.
justification.name: FacetPoint
justification.why_needed: Represents the disjoint labelled copies of points in closed facets prior to gluing the cut surface.

blocks.name: FacetPoint
blocks.text:
/-- A point of the disjoint union of the facets of `K`: a facet `F` together with a point of `F`.
-/
abbrev FacetPoint (K : Set ℝ³) : Type := Σ F : Facet K, F.1

blocks.code:
def Glued (K : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)) (p q : FacetPoint K) : Prop :=
  (p.2 : ℝ³) = q.2 ∧ ∃ v w : K.extremePoints ℝ, (edgeGraph K).Adj v w ∧ ¬ T.Adj v w ∧
    segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ⊆ p.1.1 ∧ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ⊆ q.1.1 ∧
    (p.2 : ℝ³) ∈ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w
blocks.docstring:
The elementary gluing relation on `FacetPoint K` after cutting the boundary of `K` along the
subgraph `T` of its edge graph. Two facet points are directly glued when they are copies of the
same point `x` of `K`, and `x` lies on an edge `[v, w]` of `K` which is contained in both facets
and is *not* cut, i.e. `v` and `w` are not adjacent in `T`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Relation.EqvGen`, `Setoid` / `Quotient` (used implicitly via EqvGen rather than constructing the quotient type).
justification.name: ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture.Glued
justification.why_needed: Elementary gluing relation on facet-points along uncut edges; its `Relation.EqvGen` closure defines the cut surface `P_T` as a quotient of the disjoint union of facets.

blocks.name: Glued
blocks.text:
/-- The elementary gluing relation on `FacetPoint K` after cutting the boundary of `K` along the
subgraph `T` of its edge graph. Two facet points are directly glued when they are copies of the
same point `x` of `K`, and `x` lies on an edge `[v, w]` of `K` which is contained in both facets
and is *not* cut, i.e. `v` and `w` are not adjacent in `T`. -/
def Glued (K : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)) (p q : FacetPoint K) : Prop :=
  (p.2 : ℝ³) = q.2 ∧ ∃ v w : K.extremePoints ℝ, (edgeGraph K).Adj v w ∧ ¬ T.Adj v w ∧
    segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ⊆ p.1.1 ∧ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ⊆ q.1.1 ∧
    (p.2 : ℝ³) ∈ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w

blocks.code:
def CutSurface (K : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)) : Type :=
  Quotient (Relation.EqvGen.setoid (Glued K T))
blocks.docstring:
The cut surface `K_T`: the boundary of `K` cut along the subgraph `T` of its edge graph. It
is the quotient of the disjoint union of the facets of `K` by the equivalence relation generated
by `Glued K T`, so the copies of each uncut edge are glued together (and the copies of a vertex
are identified when they are connected through uncut edges).

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `Quotient` by `Relation.EqvGen.setoid`; `CutSurface` applies it to the problem-specific gluing relation.
justification.name: CutSurface
justification.why_needed: The domain of a one-to-one unfolding must distinguish copies created by cuts while identifying all uncut edge copies.

blocks.name: CutSurface
blocks.text:
/-- The cut surface `K_T`: the boundary of `K` cut along the subgraph `T` of its edge graph. It
is the quotient of the disjoint union of the facets of `K` by the equivalence relation generated
by `Glued K T`, so the copies of each uncut edge are glued together (and the copies of a vertex
are identified when they are connected through uncut edges). -/
def CutSurface (K : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)) : Type :=
  Quotient (Relation.EqvGen.setoid (Glued K T))

blocks.code:
def IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding (K : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ))
    (u : CutSurface K T → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective u ∧
    ∀ (F : Facet K) (x y : F.1),
      dist (u (Quotient.mk _ ⟨F, x⟩)) (u (Quotient.mk _ ⟨F, y⟩)) = dist (x : ℝ³) y
blocks.docstring:
`IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding K T u` means that `u : K_T → ℝ²` is a simple (one-to-one) unfolding
of the boundary of `K` cut along `T`: `u` preserves distances between points of each facet, so
it develops every facet rigidly into the plane, and `u` is injective, so the developed facets do
not overlap (not even at boundary points which are distinct in `K_T`).

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Isometry`, `AffineIsometry` (not applicable: no isometry ℝ³ → ℝ², and each facet needs its own placement), `Set.InjOn`.
justification.name: ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture.IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding
justification.why_needed: No Mathlib notion of an isometric development/unfolding of a polyhedral surface, nor of a net; encodes facet-wise isometric placement, gluing along uncut edges, and injectivity on the cut surface.

blocks.name: IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding
blocks.text:
/-- `IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding K T u` means that `u : K_T → ℝ²` is a simple (one-to-one) unfolding
of the boundary of `K` cut along `T`: `u` preserves distances between points of each facet, so
it develops every facet rigidly into the plane, and `u` is injective, so the developed facets do
not overlap (not even at boundary points which are distinct in `K_T`). -/
def IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding (K : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ))
    (u : CutSurface K T → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective u ∧
    ∀ (F : Facet K) (x y : F.1),
      dist (u (Quotient.mk _ ⟨F, x⟩)) (u (Quotient.mk _ ⟨F, y⟩)) = dist (x : ℝ³) y

blocks.docstring:
The convex polytope `K ⊆ ℝ³` has a net (a simple edge unfolding): there is a spanning tree
`T` of the edge graph of `K` such that the boundary of `K` cut along `T` admits a one-to-one
development into the plane.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.IsTree`, `SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsSpanning` (the latter not used since a tree on the full vertex type is already spanning).
justification.name: ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture.HasNet
justification.why_needed: Packages 'there is a spanning tree of the edge graph whose edge unfolding is simple', the property asked about in the statement.

blocks.name: HasNet
blocks.text:
/-- The convex polytope `K ⊆ ℝ³` has a net (a simple edge unfolding): there is a spanning tree
`T` of the edge graph of `K` such that the boundary of `K` cut along `T` admits a one-to-one
development into the plane. -/
def HasNet (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ), T ≤ edgeGraph K ∧ T.IsTree ∧
    ∃ u : CutSurface K T → ℝ², IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding K T u

@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma IsFacet.nonempty {K F : Set ℝ³} (hF : IsFacet K F) : F.Nonempty := by
  rw [Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
  rintro rfl
  have h := hF.2
  rw [vectorSpan_empty, finrank_bot] at h
  omega
blocks.name: IsFacet.nonempty
blocks.text:
/-- A facet of `K` is nonempty. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma IsFacet.nonempty {K F : Set ℝ³} (hF : IsFacet K F) : F.Nonempty := by
  rw [Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
  rintro rfl
  have h := hF.2
  rw [vectorSpan_empty, finrank_bot] at h
  omega

lemma edgeGraph_adj {K : Set ℝ³} (v w : K.extremePoints ℝ) :

blocks.docstring:
Two vertices of `K` are adjacent in the edge graph iff they are distinct and the segment

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma Glued.symm {K : Set ℝ³} {T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)} {p q : FacetPoint K}
    (h : Glued K T p q) : Glued K T q p := by
  obtain ⟨hpq, v, w, hvw, hT, hp, hq, hmem⟩ := h
  exact ⟨hpq.symm, v, w, hvw, hT, hq, hp, hpq ▸ hmem⟩
blocks.name: Glued.symm
blocks.text:
/-- The gluing relation is symmetric. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma Glued.symm {K : Set ℝ³} {T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)} {p q : FacetPoint K}
    (h : Glued K T p q) : Glued K T q p := by
  obtain ⟨hpq, v, w, hvw, hT, hp, hq, hmem⟩ := h
  exact ⟨hpq.symm, v, w, hvw, hT, hq, hp, hpq ▸ hmem⟩

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma eqvGen_glued_snd_eq {K : Set ℝ³} {T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)}
    {p q : FacetPoint K} (h : Relation.EqvGen (Glued K T) p q) : (p.2 : ℝ³) = q.2 := by
  induction h with
  | rel _ _ h => exact h.1
  | refl _ => rfl
  | symm _ _ _ ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans _ _ _ _ _ ih₁ ih₂ => exact ih₁.trans ih₂
blocks.docstring: Points identified in the cut surface are copies of the same point of `K`.
blocks.name: eqvGen_glued_snd_eq
blocks.text:
/-- Points identified in the cut surface are copies of the same point of `K`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma eqvGen_glued_snd_eq {K : Set ℝ³} {T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)}
    {p q : FacetPoint K} (h : Relation.EqvGen (Glued K T) p q) : (p.2 : ℝ³) = q.2 := by
  induction h with
  | rel _ _ h => exact h.1
  | refl _ => rfl
  | symm _ _ _ ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans _ _ _ _ _ ih₁ ih₂ => exact ih₁.trans ih₂

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (conjectured answer 'yes'): 'net' and 'simple edge-unfolding' are synonyms here, meaning that for every compact convex polyhedron in R^3 (boundary of the convex hull of finitely many points with nonempty interior, so a genuine 3-dimensional polytope) there is a spanning tree of its edge graph such that cutting along it and developing isometrically into the plane is injective (non-overlapping, per Ghomi's 'one-to-one unfolding' convention; the boundary-touching convention should be fixed consistently); the quantifier is over all convex polyhedra, and existence is over spanning trees of actual edges only (not pseudo-edges or face subdivisions, which the article mentions as distinct, separately settled variants not posed by the statement).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates compile and share one (correct) architecture: polyhedron = convexHull of a Finset ℝ³ with nonempty interior; facets = exposed faces of vectorSpan-rank 2; edges = exposed segments between distinct extreme points; cut tree T ≤ edgeGraph with T.IsTree on the full extreme-point type (hence spanning, actual edges only); cut surface = disjoint union of facets modulo EqvGen of gluing across uncut edges; unfolding = facewise distance-preserving map to ℝ² that is injective on the cut surface (Ghomi's one-to-one convention). c06's quotient formulation (`u : CutSurface K T → ℝ²`, `Function.Injective u`, facewise `dist` preservation) is the most direct transcription of Barvinok–Ghomi's definition of an isometric embedding of a polyhedral disk and avoids junk values / separate gluing-compatibility clauses, so its declaration is the base. I edited it to use the repository's scoped `ℝ³`/`ℝ²` notation instead of bespoke Point3/Point2 abbrevs, replaced `SimpleGraph.fromRel` by the direct `edgeGraph` definition (c01/c04/c07) with a simp lemma, factored `IsFacet`/`HasNet` (c01/c04), added API lemmas adapted from c01/c02 (facet nonempty/subset/convex, Glued.symm, EqvGen preserves the underlying point), and wrote docstrings that fix the boundary-touching convention explicitly. I verified: injectivity forces faces adjacent along an uncut edge to be developed on opposite sides (same-side placement would identify relative-interior points of distinct facets, which EqvGen cannot relate since it preserves the underlying point), so any such u is the genuine developing map up to a global planar isometry; conversely Ghomi's one-to-one unfolding gives such a u. Boundary cases: empty/coplanar S excluded by nonempty interior; ∅ is not a facet (rank 0); IsTree requires a nonempty connected vertex type, satisfied by a 3-polytope. answer(True) is the conjectured positive answer.

context:
In geometry, a net of a polyhedron is an arrangement of non-overlapping edge-joined polygons in the plane that can be folded (along edges) to become the faces of the polyhedron. Polyhedral nets are a useful aid to the study of polyhedra and solid geometry in general, as they allow for physical models of polyhedra to be constructed from material such as thin cardboard.
An early instance of polyhedral nets appears in the works of Albrecht Dürer, whose 1525 book A Course in the Art of Measurement with Compass and Ruler (Unterweysung der Messung mit dem Zyrkel und Rychtscheyd) included nets for the Platonic solids and several of the Archimedean solids. These constructions were first called nets in 1543 by Augustin Hirschvogel.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Shephard's problem (a.k.a. Dürer's conjecture)

Does every convex polyhedron have a net, or simple edge-unfolding?

A (compact) convex polyhedron is the boundary of the convex hull $K$ of finitely many points of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ which do not all lie in a plane, i.e. $K$ has nonempty interior. Cutting the
boundary of $K$ along a spanning tree $T$ of the edge graph of $K$ yields a surface $K_T$: the
disjoint union of the facets of $K$, glued back together along the edges that are not in $T$.
This surface is a flat topological disk, so it can be developed isometrically into the plane.
Such a development is an *edge unfolding* of $K$. It is *simple*, and its image is a *net*, if the
developing map $K_T \to \mathbb{R}^2$ is one-to-one, i.e. the unfolded faces do not overlap.

Shephard (1975) asked whether every convex polyhedron admits a simple edge unfolding. The
conjectured answer "yes" is known as Dürer's conjecture. The problem is open.

We follow the conventions of Ghomi and Barvinok–Ghomi: an unfolding of $K_T$ is a map to the
plane which preserves distances between points of each facet, and it is simple when it is
one-to-one on all of $K_T$. In particular two distinct points of $K_T$ (for instance two copies
of a cut vertex) may not touch in the plane. The cut tree must consist of genuine edges of $K$
(not pseudo-edges, and the facets are not subdivided).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Net (polyhedron)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shephard%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sh75] Shephard, G. C., *Convex polytopes with convex nets*, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc.
  78 (1975), 389–403.
- [Gh14] Ghomi, M., *Affine unfoldings of convex polyhedra*, Geom. Topol. 18 (2014), 3055–3090.
  [arXiv:1305.3231](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.3231)
- [BG20] Barvinok, N. and Ghomi, M., *Pseudo-edge unfoldings of convex polyhedra*, Discrete
  Comput. Geom. 64 (2020), 671–689. [arXiv:1709.04944](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.04944)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

/-- `IsFacet K F` means that `F` is a facet (a two-dimensional face) of the convex polytope
`K ⊆ ℝ³`: `F` is an exposed face of `K` whose affine span is a plane. -/
def IsFacet (K F : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsExposed ℝ K F ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ F) = 2

/-- The type of facets of the convex polytope `K ⊆ ℝ³`. -/
abbrev Facet (K : Set ℝ³) : Type := {F : Set ℝ³ // IsFacet K F}

/-- The edge graph of the convex polytope `K ⊆ ℝ³`. Its vertices are the extreme points of `K`,
and two distinct vertices `v`, `w` are adjacent when the segment `[v, w]` is an exposed face of
`K`, i.e. an edge of `K`. -/
def edgeGraph (K : Set ℝ³) : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ) where
  Adj v w := v ≠ w ∧ IsExposed ℝ K (segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w)
  symm v w h := ⟨h.1.symm, segment_symm ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ▸ h.2⟩
  loopless _ h := h.1 rfl

/-- A point of the disjoint union of the facets of `K`: a facet `F` together with a point of `F`.
-/
abbrev FacetPoint (K : Set ℝ³) : Type := Σ F : Facet K, F.1

/-- The elementary gluing relation on `FacetPoint K` after cutting the boundary of `K` along the
subgraph `T` of its edge graph. Two facet points are directly glued when they are copies of the
same point `x` of `K`, and `x` lies on an edge `[v, w]` of `K` which is contained in both facets
and is *not* cut, i.e. `v` and `w` are not adjacent in `T`. -/
def Glued (K : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)) (p q : FacetPoint K) : Prop :=
  (p.2 : ℝ³) = q.2 ∧ ∃ v w : K.extremePoints ℝ, (edgeGraph K).Adj v w ∧ ¬ T.Adj v w ∧
    segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ⊆ p.1.1 ∧ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ⊆ q.1.1 ∧
    (p.2 : ℝ³) ∈ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w

/-- The cut surface `K_T`: the boundary of `K` cut along the subgraph `T` of its edge graph. It
is the quotient of the disjoint union of the facets of `K` by the equivalence relation generated
by `Glued K T`, so the copies of each uncut edge are glued together (and the copies of a vertex
are identified when they are connected through uncut edges). -/
def CutSurface (K : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)) : Type :=
  Quotient (Relation.EqvGen.setoid (Glued K T))

/-- `IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding K T u` means that `u : K_T → ℝ²` is a simple (one-to-one) unfolding
of the boundary of `K` cut along `T`: `u` preserves distances between points of each facet, so
it develops every facet rigidly into the plane, and `u` is injective, so the developed facets do
not overlap (not even at boundary points which are distinct in `K_T`). -/
def IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding (K : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ))
    (u : CutSurface K T → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective u ∧
    ∀ (F : Facet K) (x y : F.1),
      dist (u (Quotient.mk _ ⟨F, x⟩)) (u (Quotient.mk _ ⟨F, y⟩)) = dist (x : ℝ³) y

/-- The convex polytope `K ⊆ ℝ³` has a net (a simple edge unfolding): there is a spanning tree
`T` of the edge graph of `K` such that the boundary of `K` cut along `T` admits a one-to-one
development into the plane. -/
def HasNet (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ), T ≤ edgeGraph K ∧ T.IsTree ∧
    ∃ u : CutSurface K T → ℝ², IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding K T u

/-- A facet of `K` is nonempty. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma IsFacet.nonempty {K F : Set ℝ³} (hF : IsFacet K F) : F.Nonempty := by
  rw [Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
  rintro rfl
  have h := hF.2
  rw [vectorSpan_empty, finrank_bot] at h
  omega

/-- A facet of `K` is contained in `K`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma IsFacet.subset {K F : Set ℝ³} (hF : IsFacet K F) : F ⊆ K :=
  hF.1.subset

/-- A facet of a convex set `K` is convex. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma IsFacet.convex {K F : Set ℝ³} (hK : Convex ℝ K) (hF : IsFacet K F) : Convex ℝ F :=
  hF.1.convex hK

/-- Two vertices of `K` are adjacent in the edge graph iff they are distinct and the segment
between them is an exposed face of `K`. -/
@[simp, category API, AMS 52]
lemma edgeGraph_adj {K : Set ℝ³} (v w : K.extremePoints ℝ) :
    (edgeGraph K).Adj v w ↔ v ≠ w ∧ IsExposed ℝ K (segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w) :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The gluing relation is symmetric. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma Glued.symm {K : Set ℝ³} {T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)} {p q : FacetPoint K}
    (h : Glued K T p q) : Glued K T q p := by
  obtain ⟨hpq, v, w, hvw, hT, hp, hq, hmem⟩ := h
  exact ⟨hpq.symm, v, w, hvw, hT, hq, hp, hpq ▸ hmem⟩

/-- Points identified in the cut surface are copies of the same point of `K`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma eqvGen_glued_snd_eq {K : Set ℝ³} {T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)}
    {p q : FacetPoint K} (h : Relation.EqvGen (Glued K T) p q) : (p.2 : ℝ³) = q.2 := by
  induction h with
  | rel _ _ h => exact h.1
  | refl _ => rfl
  | symm _ _ _ ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans _ _ _ _ _ ih₁ ih₂ => exact ih₁.trans ih₂

/-- **Shephard's problem (Dürer's conjecture).** Does every convex polyhedron have a net, or
simple edge-unfolding? That is, for every finite set of points of $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose convex hull
$K$ has nonempty interior, is there a spanning tree $T$ of the edge graph of $K$ such that the
boundary of $K$ cut along $T$ admits a one-to-one development into the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$
(a development which is isometric on each facet and injective, so that the facets do not
overlap)? The conjectured answer is yes. -/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem shephards_problem_a_k_a_durers_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ S : Finset ℝ³, (interior (convexHull ℝ (S : Set ℝ³))).Nonempty →
      HasNet (convexHull ℝ (S : Set ℝ³)) := by
  sorry

end ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

items: A compact convex polyhedron is represented by `convexHull ℝ (V : Set Point3)` for a finite set `V`, with nonempty ordinary interior to require a genuine three-dimensional polytope. The geometric structures used later are derived intrinsically from the hull, so `V` may contain redundant generators without changing the assertion.
Facets are modeled as the two-dimensional exposed faces of the solid convex hull. For a finite-dimensional polytope these are exactly its polygonal facets.

Vertices are the extreme points of the convex hull, and actual edges are exactly the nondegenerate segments between such vertices that are exposed faces. This excludes pseudo-edges, geodesic diagonals, and face subdivisions.

A candidate cut set is a `SimpleGraph` on the full extreme-point subtype, is required to lie below the actual edge graph, and satisfies `SimpleGraph.IsTree`. Since the graph's ambient vertex type contains every polyhedron vertex, connectedness makes this a spanning tree.

The cut surface is modeled as the quotient of the disjoint union of closed facets obtained by identifying equal spatial points along precisely the actual edges outside the cut tree. Taking the equivalence closure makes the appropriate vertex-sector identifications as well.

A planar development is required to preserve Euclidean distances between every pair of points in each facet. Since every facet is convex, this is an isometric placement of each whole polygonal face; quotient well-definedness forces placements to agree along every uncut edge.

“Simple” and “non-overlapping” use Ghomi's one-to-one convention: the planar map is injective on the entire cut surface, not merely on face interiors. Thus accidental contacts between distinct boundary points are forbidden, while points intentionally identified along uncut edges remain a single domain point.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity in the source: 'non-overlapping' is not pinned down by Wikipedia; per the decomposition notes I shipped Ghomi's strict one-to-one convention (the developing map K_T → ℝ² is injective, so two distinct points of the cut surface, e.g. two copies of a cut vertex or a cut edge's interior, may not touch in the plane). The weaker 'face interiors disjoint' convention would give a formally different (weaker) statement; this choice is documented in the module and definition docstrings. Orientation-preservation (Ghomi) is not imposed but is implied up to a global reflection, which does not affect existence.
